posts.content: 72 ÷ your interest rate = how long until your money doubles 💰 This is the Rule of 72. At 7% (S&P 500 historical average): doubles in ~10 years. At 1% (national savings account average): doubles in 72 years. At 24% (average credit card APR): your debt doubles in 3 years. Same math. Completely different outcome depending on whether you're earning or owing. The gap between 1% and 7% over 30 years isn't marginal. It's the difference between falling behind inflation and building generational wealth. Simple enough to do in your head. Important enough to change how you think about every financial decision. #moneyfacts #personalfinance #investing #compoundinterest #ruleof72 #wealthbuilding #financialliteracy #financetips

Getting a raise can never lower your take-home pay 💵

Getting a raise can never lower your take-home pay 💵

Most Americans avoid raises or bonuses because they fear being 'pushed into a higher tax bracket.' This is completely wrong — and it's costing people real money.

US tax brackets are marginal. If you earn $50,000 and land in the 22% bracket, only the dollars above the previous threshold are taxed at 22%. Not your entire income. Your first $11,000 is still taxed at just 10%.

Getting a raise never decreases your take-home pay. Ever.

If you've turned down additional income over bracket fears, you've been leaving money on the table based on a myth. This is widely considered the single most expensive financial misunderstanding in America.

#moneyfacts #taxes #taxbrackets #personalfinance #myth #salaryadvice #financialliteracy #incometax

In 2023, S&P 500 companies spent $795 billion buying their own stock 📈 That's more than they paid in dividends. More than most invested in new products or employees. Here's how it works: a company uses its cash to purchase its own shares from the market. Fewer shares outstanding means each remaining share looks more valuable on paper — earnings per share goes up without any actual business growth. Executives whose compensation is tied to stock price benefit directly. Congress banned share buybacks as market manipulation until 1982, when the SEC created a safe harbor rule. Since then, US companies have spent over $10 trillion buying their own stock. The profits flow almost entirely to executives and large institutional shareholders. #moneyfacts #stockmarket #shareholder #investing #corporatefinance #economics #wealthinequality #wallstreet

Tax refunds feel like free money 💸 They're not. The average US tax refund is $3,067 — your own money, returned to you late, with zero interest paid. Every year you receive a refund, you spent the year giving the IRS an interest-free loan. Your withholding was calibrated too high. If you adjusted your W-4 and invested that $3,000 annually at the S&P 500's historical 7% average return — over a 40-year career, you'd accumulate over $650,000 in additional wealth. Refunds aren't bonuses. They're the cost of overwithholding. The tax code doesn't reward patience. It just returns the excess — months later, dollar for dollar, no gains. #moneyfacts #taxrefund #personalfinance #taxes #w4 #investing #compoundinterest #wealthbuilding #financialliteracy

$5,000 credit card debt at 24% APR, minimum payments only 💳

Result: $10,200 paid. 22 years.

You'd pay more than double the original debt — just in interest.

The minimum payment formula — typically 1-2% of the balance — is mathematically engineered to stretch your repayment as long as possible. Maximum interest revenue for the bank. Minimum progress for you.

This wasn't accidental. When minimum payments were introduced, they were specifically calibrated to optimize bank revenue.

The good news: paying even $50 extra per month cuts years off repayment and saves thousands in interest. The math is that sensitive to even small increases.

America's entire retirement system was created by accident 💼

In 1978, a benefits consultant named Ted Benna was reading the tax code and noticed a provision: section 401(k). He realized employees could use it to defer income from taxes.

He pitched the idea to his own company. They didn't want it. So he used it for his own firm instead.

The IRS approved the arrangement in 1981.

No senator designed a national retirement system. No one intended to replace pensions. One consultant found a loophole and filed some paperwork. Today, 55 million Americans depend on it for retirement.

The most important savings account in American history happened completely by accident.

#moneyfacts #401k #retirementplanning #personalfinance #investinghistory #wealthbuilding #financialfreedom #moneyhistory

Tax refunds feel like free money 💸 They're not.

The average US tax refund is $3,067 — your own money, returned to you late, with zero interest paid.

Every year you receive a refund, you spent the year giving the IRS an interest-free loan. Your withholding was calibrated too high.

If you adjusted your W-4 and invested that $3,000 annually at the S&P 500's historical 7% average return — over a 40-year career, you'd accumulate over $650,000 in additional wealth.

Refunds aren't bonuses. They're the cost of overwithholding.

The tax code doesn't reward patience. It just returns the excess — months later, dollar for dollar, no gains.
